note: The pedagogical map for V1 (panel/authoring-policy.md, 'The pedagogical map'). firstAt is the reading-order id in scope.json where the term is first defined, or null when V1 never defines it. forms are the spellings the validator matches, case-insensitive, on word boundaries, outside inline code.

terms.gloss: The file that does the thinking. One file.
terms.recap: A model is the file that does the thinking. One file.

terms.gloss: A set of machines that can talk to each other without going through anyone else.
terms.analogy: Priya's laptop, the box on the shelf and the printer.
terms.recap: A network (Book 1, ch 0) is a set of machines that can talk to each other without going through anyone else.
avoid: the internet (when your own network is meant)

terms.gloss: A skill on the map. Getting to one means you can do the thing it's named after.
terms.analogy: A circle on a London Underground line.
terms.recap: A skill on the map. Each has a colour.

terms.gloss: How much of a station has to live in your head. Grey means press go. Amber means you know what it does and why it's there, but not how to fix it. Red means you understand it well enough to tell when it's wrong.
terms.recap: Grey, press go. Amber, know what it does but not how to fix it. Red, understand it well enough to tell when it is wrong.

terms.gloss: Priya's check, the day after, of where her chat app was sending data.
terms.analogy: Going round the house to look for an open window.
terms.recap: The Wednesday check (Book 1, ch 0): look at where your chat app sends data, because nothing beeps when it goes somewhere else.

terms.gloss: The space your laptop works in; whatever it is doing right now has to be in there. Measured in gigabytes; the Settings line that says Memory or RAM.
terms.analogy: The room (the drive is the warehouse; the choir sings in the room, not the warehouse)
terms.recap: Memory (Book 1, ch 1) is the room a model has to fit in, whole, before it can speak. Your sticky-note number.
avoid: RAM as a different thing from memory

terms.gloss: The single file a model is downloaded as; the whole of the clever part in one lump. No account, no key, no phoning home. Closer to a film file than to an app.
terms.analogy: A film file: copy it to another machine with enough memory and it plays there too
terms.recap: The model file (Book 1, ch 1) is one file holding the whole model. Fits in memory or it does not run.
avoid: the model (when the file is meant)

terms.gloss: If the file is more than about three quarters of your memory number, expect a squeeze; bigger than the number, it does not run.
terms.analogy: Elbow room, because the laptop is already using some memory for being a laptop
terms.recap: Three quarters of your number is comfortable; over it is a squeeze; over the number is no.

terms.definedIn: Coach V1, Local chat (no chapter yet)
terms.gloss: A window where you type a command and the machine types back.
terms.analogy: A text message thread with your computer.
terms.recap: A terminal is a window where you type a command and the machine types back.

terms.definedIn: Coach V1, Local chat (no chapter yet)
terms.gloss: The program on the model's machine that holds the model in memory and answers questions from your chat app.
terms.analogy: The kitchen. Your chat app is the waiter.
terms.recap: A server is the program that holds the model in memory and answers. Your chat app only talks to it.

terms.definedIn: Coach V1, Local chat (no chapter yet)
terms.gloss: The name or number a machine is found by on a network, like backroom or 192.168.1.20.
terms.analogy: A house number on your street.
terms.recap: An address is the name or number a machine is found by on a network.

terms.definedIn: Coach V1, Prove it stays local (no chapter yet)
terms.gloss: The machine a program is sending data to, shown as its address.
terms.recap: A destination is where a program is sending data. Read the destinations, not the wifi icon.

terms.definedIn: Coach V1, Prove it stays local (no chapter yet)
terms.gloss: The address a machine uses to talk to itself, 127.0.0.1. Its name is localhost.
terms.analogy: Leaving yourself a note on the fridge.
terms.recap: Loopback (127.0.0.1, localhost) is a machine talking to itself. Yours.

terms.definedIn: Coach V1, Prove it stays local (no chapter yet)
terms.gloss: An address that only works inside your own network. They start 10., 192.168., or 172.16 up to 172.31.
terms.analogy: A room number inside your own building.
terms.recap: A private address only works inside your own network. Yours.

terms.definedIn: Coach V1, Prove it stays local (no chapter yet)
terms.gloss: Your own network of machines wherever they are, made with Tailscale, joining only machines you have signed in yourself. Its addresses run from 100.64 to 100.127.
terms.analogy: A private corridor between your house and your office.
terms.recap: Your tailnet is your own network across places. Its machines are yours.

terms.definedIn: Coach V1, Prove it stays local (no chapter yet)
terms.gloss: Any address that is not loopback, private or your tailnet: somebody else's machine, on the internet.
terms.analogy: A letter posted to a stranger.
terms.recap: A public address is somebody else's machine. If your chat app sends to one, the draft left the building.
